A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PosterForest research work. All 23 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original poster-generation evaluations in Table 1, a 25-participant user study in Table 2, and qualitative ablations in Section 4.5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative evaluations, user-study outcomes, ablations, and appendix qualitative results.

M1.justification: The Poster Tree construction, content and layout agents, traversal, and feedback-based refinement are unchanged. The added figure references do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 100 Paper2Poster benchmark pairs and 15 additional paper–poster pairs for qualitative evaluation and user studies. No task, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1 and 2 and the qualitative comparisons. Appendix B.5 retains the same baseline implementations, including Paper2Poster's PosterAgent variants.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C retain the same benchmark selection, model configurations, poster standardization, judging criteria, and 25-participant study with 10 evaluation sets.

E4.justification: The hierarchical Content Tree ablation, Content/Layout Agent comparisons, and clustered-figure failure case are unchanged in Figures 5–6 and A3.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 retains the same statement about fixed Python, NumPy, and PyTorch seeds. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, PosterForest-4o retains the 3.76 overall score in Table 1 and 59.2% overall preference in Table 2; appendix examples are identical.

T1.justification: The tree and node definitions and Equations (1)–(8) are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free generation, hierarchical content–layout integration, and evaluation performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including content-density problems, automated evaluation limitations, and parsing failures for densely clustered visual assets.

D1.justification: Code access information, hardware and software specifications, model details, refinement limits, and agent prompts in Appendix E are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior poster-generation and multi-agent methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds 'as shown in Figure 2' in Section 3.1 and 'as shown in Figure 3' in Section 3.3.1, linking existing explanations to existing diagrams. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the remaining prose and organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged, including appendix displays. The added references only rewrap nearby prose on pages 4–5.

improvement.justification: The two added figure references provide a small navigation convenience, but the method explanations, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices otherwise remain unchanged. These editorial additions do not create a meaningful overall quality difference.
